title: Reconcile the review's flag-day candidates into one bundle, row by row, against docs/plans/ABI-BREAK-LIST.md
summary: The reconciliation holds. Re-taken counts match (6,998 package call sites; 154 GOTO sites; 247/120 FREE/MOVABLE; ten MEGA_ICW cells, six of them handler setters), the L1 pads re-derive exactly at 386/309/232, APPEND_SYS has no caller, F2-1 is built, and abi-16 is refuted by instance.inc's own 'an index out of range is not a refusal'. The door's cycle price and both phase nets are predictions, correctly labelled. Two caveats added: the door needs an IDT gate on kern_mega and a vector held out of windowed DOS's whole-IVT bank; and byte 31 is visible to an old kernel's Sticky caption length (desksc.inc), so the API level is not quite 'ignored' by old kernels. Six doc mismatches confirmed (the K17-5 and C4 replacements reduced to facts rather than new verdicts), one already half-fixed by the doc pass.

strengths.title: Section 0 of the list is a complete flag-day checklist
strengths.why: Every reconciliation could be checked against its surfaces rather than re-derived

strengths.title: The version fence can grow a level without a bump
strengths.why: 0060:0006, header byte 31 and the class byte's spare range are each unread or bounded by their reader, so a refusal of newer-cell packages costs no flag day

strengths.title: The rare-cell bodies already are the back half of a door
strengths.why: api_rs/rsc/rx/rxc/rn take the target in BP and touch nothing else
strengths.evidence: kernel/kernel.asm OSAPI_RCELL and the api_r* bodies

findings.title: bytes-1's rare-cell door supersedes T1/K17-1, at roughly twice the cycle cost bytes-1 quoted, and forces an all-cells call macro
findings.detail: A rare cell today costs about +78 clocks over a hot SLOT. The proposed software-interrupt door adds banking, a fetch of the return CS:IP, the index read, bumping the stacked IP, the table read, kind selection, conditional IF restore and dispatch: about +150 to +215 clocks (30-45 us) per rare call on the 4.77 MHz 8088, PREDICTED, against bytes-1's +80-100. GFX_FILL_GRAY (30 sites), OSAPI_SEG (108) and FS_OP (45) need a frequency reading or promotion at the renumber. V3's XMEM trio has 7 call sites and stays recorded. K17-4 becomes ~-78 at a tripled cycle price; seven of T3's kern_small refusals cost 2 bytes each under the door and keep rule 4. Unlisted costs: `call OSAPI_X` cannot emit `int`, so all 6,998 package call sites (2,767 to rare cells) move to one OSCALL macro; os88wire.py, os88pkg.py and t_api_abi must decode `CD nn idx`; windowed DOS banks the WHOLE IVT while other tasks run, so the door vector must be held out of the exchange; the int frame adds FLAGS under CS:IP, moving abi-4's [bp+10] reader.
evidence: kernel/kernel.asm:2495-2499 OSAPI_RCELL push bp / call / dw
XMEM_RUN 2, WALK 2, SEL 3; GFX_FILL_GRAY 30; OSAPI_SEG 108; FS_OP 45
apps/dos/dos.asm:2970-2977 the whole IVT (512 words) banked
findings.recommendation: Add T5 (the door) in place of T1; keep T1 as the fallback and merge K17-1 into it. Sort the rare index by kind and measured frequency. Move the SDK to an all-cells OSCALL macro in the same commit. Measure the door on MartyPC in the final pass.
findings.bytes_est: ~-380 kern_big/kern_mega conventional, ~-240 kern_small; -2 per rare package site; +~150-215 clocks per rare call (PREDICTED)
findings.listed_as: ABI-BREAK-LIST T1, K17-1 (supersedes); K17-4; T3; T4; V3
findings.verify_note: Counts re-taken and exact: 6,998 call sites; XMEM_RUN/WALK/SEL 2/2/3; GFX_FILL_GRAY 30; OSAPI_SEG 108; FS_OP 45. OSAPI_RCELL is push bp / call / dw (kernel.asm:2495-2499). dos.asm:2970-2977 copies all 512 IVT words into dos_ivt, so the vector-exchange hazard is real. The cycle figures are a PREDICTION, labelled as such; nothing in ABI-BREAK-LIST or KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE names a software-interrupt door. One cost the reviewer did not list: on kern_mega in protected mode an `int` goes through the IDT, so the door also needs a gate there (and a selector-safe read of the return CS) - readable code selectors cover the read, not the gate.
findings.prior_art: Mac A-line trap dispatcher; DOS int 21h with retf 2 to keep CF

findings.title: Open the same door to the kernel's cw_ shims first: no ABI, and it rehearses T5
findings.detail: KERNEL-BYTE-QUEUE item 1 is stalled on BP liveness (cw_mem_disp takes the body in BP). A door that reads its operand from the return address clobbers no register and costs 3 bytes a site instead of 5 plus a 4-byte shim. build/kernel.map lists 70 cw_ symbols. Modules are versioned with the kernel, so this needs no bump, and it proves the DOS-vector, kern_mega and IF hazards before any package depends on the door.
findings.recommendation: Re-take the shim census, then implement the door for cw_ traffic only, as a kernel-private mechanism; open it to packages at the flag day only once it has held.
findings.verify_note: 70 distinct cw_ symbols in build/kernel.map confirmed; cw_mem_disp is `call bp / retf` (kernel.asm:7934). The -140 is unmeasured, and not every cw_ symbol is a shim with call sites (some are equates onto shared tails), so the census the reviewer asks for is a precondition, not a formality. A kernel-private int still sits in the vector the windowed DOS banks (gfr-1's hazard applies here first) and on kern_mega needs an IDT gate.

findings.title: abi-11's class table replaces K17-3; K17-2 survives as one runtime OSAPI_WM_FLAG door; T2-2 loses six of its ten cells
findings.detail: K17-3 (one indexed setter for ten handler words) would spend a renumber on a cell the abi-11 class table deletes. The seven window flags take AL set/clear and are per-window runtime state, so K17-2's single door survives. Of the ten MEGA_ICW* inline cells, six are handler setters and go with the table; the other four (gfx_color, osapi_seed, gfx_b1ink, ico_c1) hold kern_big's fast inline SET_COLOR path, so T2-2's remainder is refused.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite K17-3's row as the abi-11 class table; keep K17-2 as one runtime door; mark T2-2 partly superseded.
findings.bytes_est: ~-180 to -250 kern_big, ~-80 to -110 kern_small, ~-200 to -280 kern_mega conventional (ESTIMATED)
findings.listed_as: ABI-BREAK-LIST K17-3, K17-2, T2-2; abi-11, histsys-9, bytes-6
findings.verify_note: Re-read: exactly ten MEGA_ICW* cells, six MEGA_ICWB/ICWBW on W_ONSIZE/ONSZ/ONWK/ONRC/ONCLICK/ONWH and four MEGA_ICW on gfx_color, osapi_seed, gfx_b1ink, ico_c1 (line numbers have moved ~6-8 since the review). The split holds. The byte estimate is the reviewer's and unmeasured.

findings.title: No shared handle model: windows already have a stable handle; memory handles stay recorded
findings.detail: A window's BX is a pointer to a record that never moves and is readable by contract, so wm-R3's index would only hide a layout packages legitimately read. For memory, a record-offset handle (MC_SIZE 10) would be zero-translation, but kern_mega's measured forks are .cold above 1MB, and packages pay +2..4 at each of 367 FREE/MOVABLE sites, which C1 does not touch.
findings.recommendation: Record: fold hm-10 into R2-6, refuse wm-R3 while R6 is shelved; take hm-2's fence and histsys-11's wm_isrec now.
findings.verify_note: MC_SIZE 10 (memory.inc:133) and the 247/120 FREE/MOVABLE call counts re-taken exactly. R2-6 already says 'recorded - a design question larger than a flag day row', so this is consistent with the list, not a reversal of it.

findings.title: The API level goes in now, in two free places; abi-6's flag-day half and abi-16 dissolve
findings.detail: 0060:0006 is free padding with no reader. Package-header byte 31 is always 0: os88pkg.py refuses a 16-character name and any non-NUL after the terminator, and inst_set_name_x copies 15. The class byte at +15 is masked 3Fh and an index at or past SCH_NCLASS (5) launches with the largest stack rather than being refused, which refutes abi-16's 'refused as hostile'. So the kernel can publish OS88_API_LEVEL at 0060:0006 and ld_check_hdr can compare byte 31 against it with no PKG_FMT bump; mc-19's PM-clean bit fits in a free bit of +15.
evidence: tools/os88pkg.py:122-125 refuses a 16-byte name and bytes after the NUL
kernel/instance.inc:2106-2121 and bx,0x3F; out of range is not a refusal
findings.recommendation: Now: dw OS88_API_LEVEL at 0060:0006; os88pkg writes the needed level to byte 31; ld_check_hdr refuses with LD_EVER; mc-19's bit for kern_mega. Lock update without a bump. Strike abi-6's flag-day half and record abi-16 as refuted.
findings.verify_note: Every leg re-read and holds: 0x06..0x07 free (kernel.asm comment), parse_name refuses 16-char names AND non-NUL after the terminator, instance.inc:2117-2121 says verbatim 'AN INDEX OUT OF RANGE IS NOT A REFUSAL', and loader.inc's LD_H_CLASS comment says ld_check_hdr does not validate it - so abi-16 is refuted as written. Two caveats the reviewer did not state: (1) parse_name must be changed to allow byte 31, and os88face.py/os88vbt.py write the name field as 16 NUL-padded bytes; (2) an OLD kernel's desksc.inc:770-781 counts the name up to 16 bytes, so a 15-character name with a non-zero byte 31 measures 16 and falls back to its stem as a Sticky caption - harmless, but a visible difference, not 'ignored'. A class byte with bit 5 set loses its declared stack on old kernels (largest class), which is safe.
findings.prior_art: GEOS geode protocol; Windows 3.0 NE PROTMODE

findings.title: Driver cluster: histsys-7 makes D1 and drivers-9 moot; N1 re-checked for Phase 1; histsys-8 scoped and recorded; histsys-12 costs ~5 s on the XT
findings.detail: Under histsys-7's in-place reads only SOUND keeps a drv_svc copy, so drv_svcix (10 bytes) becomes a compare and drivers-9 has nothing to shrink. N1's fallbacks are still present and fail closed. A Drivers page reading titles off ~12 files costs ~12 int 13h calls, about 5 s on an XT, unless cached.
evidence: kernel/driver.inc:2981 mov ax, FSV_TAB0; :4072 mov cl, DSV_TAB0 (the 0 = 28 fallbacks)
findings.recommendation: Phase 1: N1 and histsys-7. Mark D1 superseded-if-histsys-7 and drivers-9 moot; record histsys-8 as D6, histsys-12 as D7, drivers-15 as D5.
findings.listed_as: ABI-BREAK-LIST N1, D1, D3; drivers-9, drivers-15, histsys-7, histsys-8, histsys-12
findings.verify_note: Spot-checked: both N1 fallbacks still present (driver.inc:2981, 4072 - the cited lines have moved), drv_svcix is one byte per class (10), DRV_VER 12. The D1/drivers-9 verdict is conditional on histsys-7 landing, which is itself a proposal; the ~5 s figure is ~12 x the 400 ms int 13h cost and is a prediction.

findings.title: File doors: C1 survives on correctness; C3 refuted by package-side arithmetic; C4 is half dead (APPEND_SYS has no callers)
findings.detail: C3 saves ~6 kernel bytes but adds a `mov al, mode` at each of 154 GOTO call sites (8+20+126), about +300 unpacked across packages. OSAPI_FILE_APPEND_SYS has zero callers: HDD.DRV appends system files with WRITE_SEQ+WSEQF_SYS and calls WRITE_SYS twice. Withdrawing APPEND_SYS alone removes C4's 'every caller zeroes AL' cost.
evidence: drivers/hdd/inst.inc:2240-2250 WRITE_SYS create, WRITE_SEQ + WSEQF_SYS append
findings.recommendation: Phase 2: C1, C2, and C4 as 'withdraw APPEND_SYS' only. Refuse C3. Record C9.
findings.bytes_est: C4 -17 kern_big (MEASURED spans), ~-3 kern_small; C3 net +~300
findings.verify_note: Re-grepped: no `call OSAPI_FILE_APPEND_SYS` anywhere in apps/, drivers/ or tests/; inst.inc:2240 and 3025 are the two WRITE_SYS calls. Spans: api_file_append_sys 9 bytes, dwf_dskw_append_sys 5, the jump cell 3 = 17; the cell's 3 bytes only go at a renumber, and WSEQF_SYS keeps using the shared fence (api_file_sysc), so the fence stays. GOTO site counts exact (154). C3 calls itself 'a cleanliness row', so 'refuted' is on bytes, not on its stated reason.

findings.title: L1's pad MEASURED today is 386/309/232, and L1 shares T5's flag day
findings.detail: .text+.bss ends 0xB27E / 0x80CB / 0xC918 round by KIMG_PARA to 0xB400 / 0x8200 / 0xCA00: pads of 386, 309 and 232 bytes against the row's dated 165 at build 477. FAT_SEG is KERNEL_SEG+KIMG_PARA on every ROM_COLD kernel.
evidence: kernel/kernel.asm:1668 KIMG_PARA; :1804 FAT_SEG equ KERNEL_SEG + KIMG_PARA under %ifdef ROM_COLD
findings.recommendation: Refresh L1's figure (dated, variable, ~256 average) and schedule it in the same Phase 2 commit as T5.
findings.verify_note: Arithmetic re-done off the three maps in build/ (Nov 8 03:08-03:11): 0xB400-0xB27E=386, 0x8200-0x80CB=309, 0xCA00-0xC918=232. KIMG_PARA rounds .text+.bss to 512 (kernel.asm:1668) and FAT_SEG follows it in the ROM_COLD arm (:1804). The figure moves with every commit, as the reviewer says.

findings.title: Every other flag-day finding placed under a list letter
findings.detail: New rows R9, T6, R10, R11, R12, A4, A5, F3, P3; folds into existing rows V1, L3, P2, F2, V2.
findings.recommendation: Add the new rows and cross-references to ABI-BREAK-LIST.
findings.listed_as: ABI-BREAK-LIST T, R, C, D, F, A, P, V1, V2, L3, P2, F2
findings.verify_note: Not re-derived row by row (low, bookkeeping). Spot-check: none of T5, R9, C9 or an API-level row exists in the list today, so the new ids do not collide.

findings.title: Phase 1 and Phase 2 written out, with a net per kernel
findings.detail: Phase 1 (now, no bump) and Phase 2 (PKG_FMT 10->13, DRV_VER 12->14) batches with ESTIMATED nets: Phase 1 ~-260 kern_big, ~-35 kern_small, ~-125 kern_mega; Phase 2 ~-1,078 / ~-685 / ~-957 conventional.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the two batches as the plan of record and quote the nets as ESTIMATED until the door and class table are measured on build spans.
findings.verify_note: PKG_FMT 10 and DRV_VER 12 confirmed. The nets are sums of estimates, about a third of them L1's variable pad and ~140 of Phase 1's kern_big figure gfr-2's unmeasured cw_ door; they are planning figures, correctly labelled.
